lesson_scope: Equilibrium of four or more coplanar forces acting at a point; simultaneous linear and trigonometric equations for two or more unknown forces or angles; resolution along chosen perpendicular axes; symmetrical and asymmetrical multi-string suspensions; equilibrium on inclined planes under multiple external forces; and analysis of limiting conditions such as strings becoming slack.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 1: Axial four-force equilibrium with two independent unknowns

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Axial four-force equilibrium with two independent unknowns

hints: In equilibrium, the sum of forces along each axis must be zero independently: $\Sigma F_x = 0$ and $\Sigma F_y = 0$.
Set $P = 25\text{ N}$ to balance the horizontal pull, and $Q = 18\text{ N}$ to balance the vertical pull.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the horizontal equilibrium equation:
$$\Sigma F_x = 25 - P = 0 \implies P = 25\text{ N}$$

Set up the vertical equilibrium equation:
$$\Sigma F_y = 18 - Q = 0 \implies Q = 18\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Look at each axis independently:
- Horizontal forces: $+25\text{ N}$ rightwards and $-P$ leftwards.
- Vertical forces: $+18\text{ N}$ upwards and $-Q$ downwards.
Write down the balance statements:
$$\Sigma F_x = 0 \implies P = 25\text{ N}, \quad \Sigma F_y = 0 \implies Q = 18\text{ N}$$

Confirm the result:
$$P = 25\text{ N}, \quad Q = 18\text{ N}$$
Each unknown force directly opposes and cancels one known force.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies equilibrium condition along each axis: $25 - P = 0$ and $18 - Q = 0$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 2: Two unknown angled forces balancing vertical load

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 2: Two unknown angled forces balancing vertical load

hints: Resolve horizontally: $P\cos 30^\circ = Q\cos 60^\circ$, which gives $P\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = Q\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \implies Q = P\sqrt{3}$.
Resolve vertically: $P\sin 30^\circ + Q\sin 60^\circ = 40$. Substitute $Q = P\sqrt{3}$ to find $P = 20\text{ N}$ and $Q = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.6\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_x = P\cos 30^\circ - Q\cos 60^\circ = 0$$
$$P\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = Q\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \implies Q = P\sqrt{3}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium and substitute $Q$:
$$\Sigma F_y = P\sin 30^\circ + Q\sin 60^\circ - 40 = 0$$
$$P(0.5) + (P\sqrt{3})\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 40$$
$$0.5 P + 1.5 P = 40 \implies 2 P = 40 \implies P = 20\text{ N}$$
$$Q = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.641 \approx 34.6\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Link the two unknown forces using horizontal cancellation:
- Force $P$ pulls rightwards with component $P\cos 30^\circ$.
- Force $Q$ pulls leftwards with component $Q\cos 60^\circ$.
Equate them:
$$P\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = Q\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \implies Q = P\sqrt{3}$$

Solve for both magnitudes using vertical equilibrium:
- Both upward components combine to support the $40\text{ N}$ load:
$$P\sin 30^\circ + Q\sin 60^\circ = 40\text{ N}$$
Substitute $Q = P\sqrt{3}$:
$$0.5P + 1.5P = 40 \implies P = 20\text{ N}, \quad Q = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.6\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves horizontally to get $P\cos 30^\circ = Q\cos 60^\circ \implies Q = P\sqrt{3}$ and substitutes into vertical equation $P\sin 30^\circ + Q\sin 60^\circ = 40$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 3: Fourth balancing force for three perpendicular forces

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 3: Fourth balancing force for three perpendicular forces

hints: Sum the forces along $x$: $10 - 30 + F_x = 0 \implies F_x = 20\text{ N}$.
Sum the forces along $y$: $20 + F_y = 0 \implies F_y = -20\text{ N}$, then find magnitude $|\mathbf{F}| = \sqrt{20^2 + 20^2} = 20\sqrt{2}\text{ N}$ and direction $\theta = 45^\circ$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the rectangular components of $\mathbf{F}$ from equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_x = 10 - 30 + F_x = 0 \implies F_x = 20\text{ N}$$
$$\Sigma F_y = 20 + F_y = 0 \implies F_y = -20\text{ N}$$

Calculate the magnitude and direction of $\mathbf{F}$:
$$|\mathbf{F}| = \sqrt{20^2 + (-20)^2} = \sqrt{400 + 400} = \sqrt{800} = 20\sqrt{2} \approx 28.284 \approx 28.3\text{ N}$$
$$\tan\theta = \frac{|F_y|}{|F_x|} = \frac{20}{20} = 1 \implies \theta = 45^\circ$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Sum the three known forces first:
- Horizontal net pull: $10 - 30 = -20\text{ N}$ (net pull is $20\text{ N}$ leftwards).
- Vertical net pull: $+20\text{ N}$ (upwards).
To achieve equilibrium, force $\mathbf{F}$ must cancel both:
$$F_x = +20\text{ N}, \quad F_y = -20\text{ N}$$

Compute the resultant magnitude and direction:
- Magnitude from Pythagoras:
$$|\mathbf{F}| = \sqrt{20^2 + 20^2} = 20\sqrt{2} \approx 28.3\text{ N}$$
- Direction angle below the positive $x$-axis:
$$\theta = \arctan(1) = 45^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves horizontally and vertically: $F_x + 10 - 30 = 0 \implies F_x = 20$ and $F_y + 20 = 0 \implies F_y = -20$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 4: Symmetrical two-string suspension under gravity

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 4: Symmetrical two-string suspension under gravity

hints: By symmetry, horizontal components cancel ($T_1\cos 45^\circ = T_2\cos 45^\circ$), so the two tensions are equal: $T_1 = T_2 = T$.
Resolve vertically: $2 T\sin 45^\circ = 50\sqrt{2}$. Since $\sin 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, we have $T\sqrt{2} = 50\sqrt{2} \implies T = 50\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply horizontal symmetry to equate the string tensions:
$$\Sigma F_x = T_1\cos 45^\circ - T_2\cos 45^\circ = 0 \implies T_1 = T_2 = T$$

Resolve vertically in equilibrium to find $T$:
$$\Sigma F_y = 2 T\sin 45^\circ - 50\sqrt{2} = 0$$
$$2 T\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 50\sqrt{2} \implies T\sqrt{2} = 50\sqrt{2} \implies T = 50\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Recognize the geometric symmetry:
- Both strings pull at the same angle $45^\circ$ on opposite sides.
- Horizontal balance requires the tensions to be equal:
$$T_1 = T_2 = T$$

Balance the vertical forces:
- Each string contributes an upward pull of $T\sin 45^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}T$.
- Their combined upward support balances the weight:
$$2\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}T\right) = 50\sqrt{2} \implies T\sqrt{2} = 50\sqrt{2} \implies T = 50\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies symmetry to deduce equal tensions and sets up vertical equilibrium: $2 T\sin 45^\circ = 50\sqrt{2}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 5: Unknown magnitude and angle in multi-force equilibrium

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 5: Unknown magnitude and angle in multi-force equilibrium

hints: Find the components of force $\mathbf{P}$ required for equilibrium: $P_x = 35 - 15 = 20\text{ N}$ and $P_y = -25\text{ N}$.
Calculate the magnitude $P = \sqrt{20^2 + 25^2} = \sqrt{1025} \approx 32.0\text{ N}$, and find the angle with the vertical using $\tan\theta = \frac{20}{25} = 0.8$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the horizontal and vertical components of $\mathbf{P}$:
$$\Sigma F_x = 15 - 35 + P_x = 0 \implies P_x = 20\text{ N}$$
$$\Sigma F_y = 25 + P_y = 0 \implies P_y = -25\text{ N}$$

Calculate the magnitude and direction angle with the vertical:
$$P = \sqrt{20^2 + (-25)^2} = \sqrt{400 + 625} = \sqrt{1025} = 5\sqrt{41} \approx 32.0156 \approx 32.0\text{ N}$$
$$\tan\theta = \frac{|P_x|}{|P_y|} = \frac{20}{25} = 0.8 \implies \theta = \arctan(0.8) \approx 38.6598^\circ \approx 38.7^\circ$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Combine the known orthogonal forces first:
- Net horizontal force: $15 - 35 = -20\text{ N}$ (leftwards).
- Net vertical force: $+25\text{ N}$ (upwards).
To cancel this net force, $\mathbf{P}$ must pull rightwards and downwards:
$$P_x = 20\text{ N}, \quad P_y = -25\text{ N}$$

Calculate the magnitude $P$ and angle with the vertical:
- Hypotenuse magnitude:
$$P = \sqrt{20^2 + 25^2} = \sqrt{1025} = 5\sqrt{41} \approx 32.0\text{ N}$$
- Angle $\theta$ from the downward vertical line:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{20}{25} = 0.8 \implies \theta = \arctan(0.8) \approx 38.7^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves horizontally and vertically: $P_x + 15 - 35 = 0 \implies P_x = 20$ and $P_y + 25 = 0 \implies P_y = -25$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 6: Decoupled two-unknown system with orthogonal separation

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 6: Decoupled two-unknown system with orthogonal separation

hints: Notice that $P$ is purely horizontal and $Q$ is purely vertical, so each unknown can be solved separately from one axis equation.

Resolve horizontally: $P = 40\cos 30^\circ + 60\cos 60^\circ = 20\sqrt{3} + 30 \approx 64.6\text{ N}$. Resolve vertically: $Q = 40\sin 30^\circ + 60\sin 60^\circ = 20 + 30\sqrt{3} \approx 72.0\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_x = P - 40\cos 30^\circ - 60\cos 60^\circ = 0$$
$$P = 40\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + 60(0.5) = 20\sqrt{3} + 30 \approx 34.641 + 30 = 64.641 \approx 64.6\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_y = Q - 40\sin 30^\circ - 60\sin 60^\circ = 0$$
$$Q = 40(0.5) + 60\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 20 + 30\sqrt{3} \approx 20 + 51.9615 = 71.9615 \approx 72.0\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Notice the advantage of orthogonal unknown forces:
- Because $P$ acts purely along the $x$-axis, it does not appear in the vertical equation.
- Because $Q$ acts purely along the $y$-axis, it does not appear in the horizontal equation.
The two balance equations are completely decoupled:
$$\Sigma F_x = 0, \quad \Sigma F_y = 0$$

Evaluate the sums directly:
- Horizontal balance:
$$P = 40\cos 30^\circ + 60\cos 60^\circ = 20\sqrt{3} + 30 \approx 64.6\text{ N}$$
- Vertical balance:
$$Q = 40\sin 30^\circ + 60\sin 60^\circ = 20 + 30\sqrt{3} \approx 72.0\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves vertically: $Q = 40\sin 30^\circ + 60\sin 60^\circ = 20 + 30\sqrt{3}$ to obtain $P \approx 64.6\text{ N}$ and $Q \approx 72.0\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Core Practice 1: Two-string ceiling suspension with complementary angles

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 1: Two-string ceiling suspension with complementary angles

hints: Resolve horizontally: the leftward component of $T_1$ must balance the rightward component of $T_2$: $T_1\cos 30^\circ = T_2\cos 60^\circ$.
Resolve vertically: the sum of the upward vertical components of both tensions must support the weight of the particle: $T_1\sin 30^\circ + T_2\sin 60^\circ = 4(10) = 40\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_x = T_2\cos 60^\circ - T_1\cos 30^\circ = 0 \implies T_1\cos 30^\circ = T_2\cos 60^\circ$$
$$T_1\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = T_2\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \implies T_2 = \sqrt{3} T_1$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_y = T_1\sin 30^\circ + T_2\sin 60^\circ - mg = 0$$
$$T_1\sin 30^\circ + T_2\sin 60^\circ = 4(10) = 40$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Form the horizontal balance equation:
- String 1 pulls to the left with component $T_1\cos 30^\circ$.
- String 2 pulls to the right with component $T_2\cos 60^\circ$.
Equate them for equilibrium:
$$T_1\cos 30^\circ = T_2\cos 60^\circ \implies T_2 = \sqrt{3} T_1$$

Form the vertical balance equation:
- The total downward gravitational load is $W = mg = 4 \times 10 = 40\text{ N}$.
- Both strings pull upwards to share this load:
$$T_1\sin 30^\circ + T_2\sin 60^\circ = 40\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves horizontally in equilibrium: $T_1\cos 30^\circ = T_2\cos 60^\circ$ (or $T_2 = \sqrt{3} T_1$).
Resolves vertically in equilibrium: $T_1\sin 30^\circ + T_2\sin 60^\circ = mg = 40\text{ N}$.

hints: Substitute $T_2 = \sqrt{3} T_1$ directly into the vertical equation from part (a).
Simplify: $T_1(0.5) + 1.5 T_1 = 2 T_1 = 40 \implies T_1 = 20\text{ N}$, then find $T_2 = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.6\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $T_2 = \sqrt{3} T_1$ into the vertical equilibrium equation:
$$T_1\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) + (\sqrt{3} T_1)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 40$$
$$\frac{1}{2} T_1 + \frac{3}{2} T_1 = 40 \implies 2 T_1 = 40$$

Solve for $T_1$ and $T_2$:
$$T_1 = \frac{40}{2} = 20\text{ N}$$
$$T_2 = \sqrt{3}(20) = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.641 \approx 34.6\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Combine the two equations by substitution:
- Replace $T_2$ with $\sqrt{3}T_1$ in the vertical balance equation:
$$\frac{1}{2}T_1 + \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)(\sqrt{3}T_1) = 40$$
$$\frac{1}{2}T_1 + \frac{3}{2}T_1 = 2T_1 = 40\text{ N}$$

Evaluate both tensions:
- Tension in string 1:
$$T_1 = \frac{40}{2} = 20\text{ N}$$
- Tension in string 2:
$$T_2 = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.6\text{ N}$$
Notice that because string 2 is steeper ($60^\circ$ versus $30^\circ$), it supports more of the vertical load.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 2: Four coplanar forces with staggered unknown resolution

hints: Notice that forces $50\text{ N}$ and $P$ are both horizontal, so only the $60\text{ N}$ force and force $Q$ have vertical components.
Set the upward vertical force equal to the downward vertical component: $60 = Q\sin 30^\circ \implies Q = \frac{60}{0.5} = 120\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_y = 60 - Q\sin 30^\circ = 0 \implies Q\sin 30^\circ = 60$$

Solve for the magnitude $Q$:
$$Q(0.5) = 60 \implies Q = \frac{60}{0.5} = 120\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Isolate the vertical axis first:
- The only upward force is the $60\text{ N}$ pull along $+y$.
- The only downward force component comes from force $Q$, which pulls at $30^\circ$ below the horizontal.
- Neither the $50\text{ N}$ force nor force $P$ contributes vertically.
Write the vertical balance:
$$\Sigma F_y = 0 \implies Q\sin 30^\circ = 60\text{ N}$$

Solve for $Q$:
$$Q = \frac{60}{\sin 30^\circ} = \frac{60}{0.5} = 120\text{ N}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 2: Four coplanar forces with staggered unknown resolution

hints: Resolve horizontally: force $P$ acts in the negative $x$-direction and must balance the two rightward forces: $50\text{ N}$ and $Q\cos 30^\circ$.
Substitute $Q = 120\text{ N}$ into $P = 50 + 120\cos 30^\circ = 50 + 120\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 50 + 60\sqrt{3} \approx 154\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_x = 50 + Q\cos 30^\circ - P = 0 \implies P = 50 + Q\cos 30^\circ$$

Substitute $Q = 120\text{ N}$ and evaluate $P$:
$$P = 50 + 120\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 50 + 60\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$
$$P \approx 50 + 60(1.73205) = 50 + 103.923 = 153.923 \approx 154\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Now examine the horizontal axis:
- Pulls to the right: the $50\text{ N}$ force plus the horizontal component of force $Q$, which is $Q\cos 30^\circ$.
- Pulls to the left: force $P$.
Equate rightward and leftward pulls:
$$P = 50 + Q\cos 30^\circ$$

Substitute the value of $Q = 120\text{ N}$ found in part (a):
$$P = 50 + 120\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 50 + 60\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$
$$P \approx 50 + 103.92 = 154\text{ N}$$
The horizontal force $P$ must be $154\text{ N}$ to balance both rightward forces.

hints: Resolve horizontally: the rightward component $40\cos 30^\circ$ must balance the two leftward components $30\cos 45^\circ$ and $P\cos\theta$.
Set up the horizontal equation: $P\cos\theta = 40\cos 30^\circ - 30\cos 45^\circ \approx 34.641 - 21.213 = 13.428\text{ N}$.

Resolve vertically: the two upward components $40\sin 30^\circ$ and $30\sin 45^\circ$ balance the downward force of $15\text{ N}$ and $P\sin\theta$, so $P\sin\theta = 20 + 21.213 - 15 = 26.213\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_x = 40\cos 30^\circ - 30\cos 45^\circ - P\cos\theta = 0$$
$$P\cos\theta = 40\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) - 30\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 20\sqrt{3} - 15\sqrt{2}$$
$$P\cos\theta \approx 34.6410 - 21.2132 = 13.4278 \approx 13.428\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_y = 40\sin 30^\circ + 30\sin 45^\circ - 15 - P\sin\theta = 0$$
$$P\sin\theta = 40(0.5) + 30\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) - 15 = 20 + 15\sqrt{2} - 15 = 5 + 15\sqrt{2}$$
$$P\sin\theta \approx 5 + 21.2132 = 26.2132 \approx 26.213\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Group the horizontal components by direction:
- Rightward pulls: $40\cos 30^\circ \approx 34.641\text{ N}$.
- Leftward pulls: $30\cos 45^\circ \approx 21.213\text{ N}$ and $P\cos\theta$.
Equate them for equilibrium:
$$P\cos\theta = 40\cos 30^\circ - 30\cos 45^\circ \approx 13.428\text{ N}$$

Group the vertical components by direction:
- Upward pulls: $40\sin 30^\circ = 20\text{ N}$ and $30\sin 45^\circ \approx 21.213\text{ N}$ (total upward $\approx 41.213\text{ N}$).
- Downward pulls: $15\text{ N}$ and $P\sin\theta$.
Equate upward and downward pulls:
$$P\sin\theta = 20 + 21.213 - 15 = 26.213\text{ N}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Core Practice 4: Asymmetric two-string suspension with horizontal force

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 4: Asymmetric two-string suspension with horizontal force

hints: String $A$ pulls to the left with horizontal component $T_A\sin 40^\circ$. String $B$ pulls to the right with component $T_B\sin 50^\circ$, and the horizontal push is $10\text{ N}$ to the right.
Form the horizontal balance equation: $T_A\sin 40^\circ = T_B\sin 50^\circ + 10 \implies T_A\sin 40^\circ - T_B\sin 50^\circ = 10$.
Form the vertical balance equation: both strings pull upwards to support the $50\text{ N}$ weight: $T_A\cos 40^\circ + T_B\cos 50^\circ = 50$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium (taking leftwards as positive for $T_A$):
$$\Sigma F_x = T_A\sin 40^\circ - T_B\sin 50^\circ - 10 = 0$$
$$T_A\sin 40^\circ - T_B\sin 50^\circ = 10$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium (taking upwards as positive):
$$\Sigma F_y = T_A\cos 40^\circ + T_B\cos 50^\circ - 50 = 0$$
$$T_A\cos 40^\circ + T_B\cos 50^\circ = 50$$

Notice the trigonometric relationship between complementary angles:
$$\sin 50^\circ = \cos 40^\circ \approx 0.7660, \quad \cos 50^\circ = \sin 40^\circ \approx 0.6428$$
This means the two strings are perpendicular: $40^\circ + 50^\circ = 90^\circ$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up horizontal balance:
- Pulling left: string $A$ with component $T_A\sin 40^\circ$.
- Pulling right: string $B$ with component $T_B\sin 50^\circ$, and the applied horizontal push of $10\text{ N}$.
Equate leftward and rightward forces:
$$T_A\sin 40^\circ - T_B\sin 50^\circ = 10\text{ N}$$

Set up vertical balance:
- The downward weight is $50\text{ N}$.
- Both strings contribute upward support:
$$T_A\cos 40^\circ + T_B\cos 50^\circ = 50\text{ N}$$

Observe the orthogonal structure:
- Because $40^\circ + 50^\circ = 90^\circ$, the two strings meet at a right angle:
$$\sin 50^\circ = \cos 40^\circ, \quad \cos 50^\circ = \sin 40^\circ$$
This complementary symmetry allows clean simultaneous elimination.

ai_rubric.observable: Notes that $\sin 50^\circ = \cos 40^\circ$ and $\cos 50^\circ = \sin 40^\circ$, confirming perpendicular string geometry.

hints: Multiply the first equation by $\sin 40^\circ$ and the second equation by $\cos 40^\circ$, then add them.
Since $\sin 50^\circ = \cos 40^\circ$ and $\cos 50^\circ = \sin 40^\circ$, the $T_B$ terms cancel out completely: $T_A(\sin^2 40^\circ + \cos^2 40^\circ) = 10\sin 40^\circ + 50\cos 40^\circ$.
Compute $T_A = 10(0.6428) + 50(0.7660) = 44.7\text{ N}$, and find $T_B = 50\sin 40^\circ - 10\cos 40^\circ = 24.5\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Write the system using $c = \cos 40^\circ = \sin 50^\circ \approx 0.76604$ and $s = \sin 40^\circ = \cos 50^\circ \approx 0.64279$:
$$(1) \quad s T_A - c T_B = 10$$
$$(2) \quad c T_A + s T_B = 50$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Solve the linear simultaneous system by orthogonal projection:
- Equation 1: $0.6428 T_A - 0.7660 T_B = 10$
- Equation 2: $0.7660 T_A + 0.6428 T_B = 50$
Multiply (1) by $0.6428$ and (2) by $0.7660$ and sum them:
$$T_A = 10\sin 40^\circ + 50\cos 40^\circ$$

Calculate tension $T_A$:
$$T_A = 6.428 + 38.302 = 44.730 \approx 44.7\text{ N}$$

Calculate tension $T_B$:
$$T_B = 50\sin 40^\circ - 10\cos 40^\circ = 32.139 - 7.660 = 24.479 \approx 24.5\text{ N}$$
The horizontal push of $10\text{ N}$ to the right increases the tension in string $A$ to $44.7\text{ N}$ while reducing the tension in string $B$ to $24.5\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Multiplies equations by coefficients to eliminate one variable, or substitutes using numerical trig values.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 5: Smooth inclined plane with horizontal push and parallel holding force

hints: Choose axes parallel and perpendicular to the inclined plane.
The component of the horizontal force $H$ acting up the plane is $H\cos 30^\circ$.
The component of weight $W = mg = 3(10) = 30\text{ N}$ down the plane is $30\sin 30^\circ = 15\text{ N}$. Set $F + H\cos 30^\circ = 15$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the weight of the particle:
$$W = mg = 3(10) = 30\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces parallel to the plane in equilibrium (upwards as positive):
$$\Sigma F_\parallel = F + H\cos 30^\circ - mg\sin 30^\circ = 0$$
$$F = 30\sin 30^\circ - H\cos 30^\circ = 30(0.5) - H\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 15 - H\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up axes aligned with the incline:
- Parallel to the incline (up the slope is positive).
- Perpendicular to the incline (away from the surface is positive).
The weight is $30\text{ N}$ downwards:
$$W = mg = 3(10) = 30\text{ N}$$

Balance forces up and down the slope:
- Down the slope: gravitational pull $30\sin 30^\circ = 15\text{ N}$.
- Up the slope: pulling force $F$, plus the upward slope component of horizontal push $H\cos 30^\circ$.
Equate them for equilibrium:
$$F + H\cos 30^\circ = 15 \implies F = 15 - H\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves parallel to the plane: $F + H\cos 30^\circ - mg\sin 30^\circ = 0$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:

$$F_\text{press} = 30\cos 30^\circ + 10\sin 30^\circ$$

Set the normal reaction equal to the total pressing force:
$$R_N = 30\cos 30^\circ + 10\sin 30^\circ = 15\sqrt{3} + 5\text{ N}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 1: Five coplanar forces in equilibrium with multiple surds

hints: Notice that force $P$ is purely vertical, so resolving horizontally isolates unknown force $Q$ directly.
Sum all horizontal components: $30 + 40\cos 60^\circ - 25\sqrt{2}\cos 45^\circ - Q\cos 30^\circ = 0$.
Evaluate the known values: $40\cos 60^\circ = 20\text{ N}$ and $25\sqrt{2}\cos 45^\circ = 25\text{ N}$, yielding $30 + 20 - 25 = 25\text{ N}$.
Equate $Q\cos 30^\circ = 25 \implies Q\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 25 \implies Q = \frac{50}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{50\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 28.9\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the horizontal equilibrium equation:
$$\Sigma F_x = 30 + 40\cos 60^\circ - 25\sqrt{2}\cos 45^\circ - Q\cos 30^\circ = 0$$

Evaluate the trigonometric constants for the known forces:
$$40\cos 60^\circ = 40(0.5) = 20\text{ N}$$
$$25\sqrt{2}\cos 45^\circ = 25\sqrt{2}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 25\text{ N}$$
$$30 + 20 - 25 - Q\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 0 \implies 25 = Q\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$$

Solve for $Q$ in exact surd form and evaluate numerically:
$$Q = \frac{50}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{50\sqrt{3}}{3}\text{ N} \approx 28.8675 \approx 28.9\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Examine the five forces horizontally:
- Force $\mathbf{F}_1$: $+30\text{ N}$.
- Force $\mathbf{F}_2$: $+40\cos 60^\circ = +20\text{ N}$.
- Force $\mathbf{F}_3$: $-25\sqrt{2}\cos 45^\circ = -25\text{ N}$.
- Force $\mathbf{F}_4$: $0\text{ N}$ (purely vertical).
- Force $\mathbf{F}_5$: $-Q\cos 30^\circ$.
Write the horizontal balance equation:
$$30 + 20 - 25 - Q\cos 30^\circ = 0$$

Simplify the net known horizontal pull:
$$25 - Q\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 0 \implies Q = \frac{50}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{50\sqrt{3}}{3}\text{ N}$$

State the magnitude of force $Q$:
$$Q = \frac{50\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 28.9\text{ N}$$
This precise magnitude balances the horizontal pull of the other forces.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 1: Five coplanar forces in equilibrium with multiple surds

hints: Resolve vertically: the upward components $40\sin 60^\circ$ and $25\sqrt{2}\sin 45^\circ$ balance the downward force $P$ and the downward component $Q\sin 30^\circ$.
Form the vertical balance equation: $P = 40\sin 60^\circ + 25\sqrt{2}\sin 45^\circ - Q\sin 30^\circ$.
Substitute $Q = \frac{50\sqrt{3}}{3}$ and $\sin 30^\circ = 0.5$ to get $Q\sin 30^\circ = \frac{25\sqrt{3}}{3}$.
Combine the $\sqrt{3}$ terms: $20\sqrt{3} - \frac{25\sqrt{3}}{3} = \frac{35\sqrt{3}}{3}$, so $P = 25 + \frac{35\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 45.2\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the vertical equilibrium equation:
$$\Sigma F_y = 40\sin 60^\circ + 25\sqrt{2}\sin 45^\circ - P - Q\sin 30^\circ = 0$$
$$P = 40\sin 60^\circ + 25\sqrt{2}\sin 45^\circ - Q\sin 30^\circ$$

Evaluate the upward vertical components:
$$40\sin 60^\circ = 40\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 20\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$
$$25\sqrt{2}\sin 45^\circ = 25\sqrt{2}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 25\text{ N}$$

Substitute $Q = \frac{50\sqrt{3}}{3}$ and evaluate the downward component:
$$Q\sin 30^\circ = \left(\frac{50\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{25\sqrt{3}}{3}\text{ N}$$

Combine terms into exact surd form and find the numerical value:
$$P = 25 + 20\sqrt{3} - \frac{25\sqrt{3}}{3} = 25 + \frac{60\sqrt{3} - 25\sqrt{3}}{3} = 25 + \frac{35\sqrt{3}}{3}\text{ N}$$
$$P \approx 25 + \frac{35(1.73205)}{3} = 25 + 20.2073 = 45.2073 \approx 45.2\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Group all vertical components:
- Upward pulls: $40\sin 60^\circ = 20\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$ and $25\sqrt{2}\sin 45^\circ = 25\text{ N}$.
- Downward pulls: force $P$ along $-y$, plus the downward component $Q\sin 30^\circ$.
Equate upward and downward forces:
$$P + Q\sin 30^\circ = 25 + 20\sqrt{3}$$

Substitute the value of $Q = \frac{50\sqrt{3}}{3}$ found in part (a):
$$Q\sin 30^\circ = \frac{50\sqrt{3}}{3} \times 0.5 = \frac{25\sqrt{3}}{3}$$

Isolate $P$ and collect the radical terms:
$$P = 25 + \left(20 - \frac{25}{3}\right)\sqrt{3} = 25 + \frac{35\sqrt{3}}{3}\text{ N}$$

Compute the numerical magnitude:
$$P \approx 25 + 20.21 = 45.2\text{ N}$$
The vertical balancing force $P$ must be $45.2\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves vertically in equilibrium: $40\sin 60^\circ + 25\sqrt{2}\sin 45^\circ - P - Q\sin 30^\circ = 0$.
Simplifies to exact surd form $P = 25 + \frac{35\sqrt{3}}{3}\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 2: Multi-string junction under variable horizontal load and slack condition

hints: Resolve horizontally: string $OA$ pulls to the left ($T_A\cos 60^\circ$), while string $OB$ ($T_B\cos 30^\circ$) and the force $P$ pull to the right.
Form the horizontal equation: $0.5 T_A - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} T_B = P \implies T_A - \sqrt{3} T_B = 2P$.
Resolve vertically: $T_A\sin 60^\circ + T_B\sin 30^\circ = 5(10) = 50 \implies \sqrt{3} T_A + T_B = 100$.
Multiply the vertical equation by $\sqrt{3}$ and add to the horizontal equation to find $T_A = 0.5 P + 25\sqrt{3}$, then deduce $T_B = 25 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} P$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_x = T_A\cos 60^\circ - T_B\cos 30^\circ - P = 0$$
$$T_A(0.5) - T_B\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = P \implies T_A - \sqrt{3} T_B = 2P \quad \text{--- (1)}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_y = T_A\sin 60^\circ + T_B\sin 30^\circ - mg = 0$$
$$T_A\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + T_B(0.5) = 50 \implies \sqrt{3} T_A + T_B = 100 \quad \text{--- (2)}$$

Multiply (2) by $\sqrt{3}$ and add to (1):
$$\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3} T_A + T_B) = 3 T_A + \sqrt{3} T_B = 100\sqrt{3}$$
$$(T_A - \sqrt{3} T_B) + (3 T_A + \sqrt{3} T_B) = 2P + 100\sqrt{3}$$
$$4 T_A = 2P + 100\sqrt{3} \implies T_A = 0.5 P + 25\sqrt{3}$$

Substitute $T_A$ into (2) to find $T_B$:
$$T_B = 100 - \sqrt{3} T_A = 100 - \sqrt{3}(0.5 P + 25\sqrt{3}) = 100 - 75 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} P = 25 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} P$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Analyze the forces acting at junction $O$:
- Weight acts vertically downwards: $W = mg = 5 \times 10 = 50\text{ N}$.
- String $OA$ pulls upwards and leftwards at $60^\circ$ to the ceiling.
- String $OB$ pulls upwards and rightwards at $30^\circ$ to the ceiling.
- Applied force $P$ pulls horizontally rightwards:
$$\mathbf{W} = -50\mathbf{j}, \quad \mathbf{P} = P\mathbf{i}$$

Write the simultaneous balance equations:
- Horizontal axis:
$$\frac{1}{2}T_A - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}T_B = P$$
- Vertical axis:
$$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}T_A + \frac{1}{2}T_B = 50$$

Solve for each tension in terms of $P$:
- For $T_A$:
$$T_A = 0.5 P + 25\sqrt{3}$$
- For $T_B$:
$$T_B = 25 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} P$$
Notice that as $P$ increases, string $OA$ becomes tighter while string $OB$ loses tension.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves horizontally in equilibrium: $T_A\cos 60^\circ - T_B\cos 30^\circ = P$.
Resolves vertically in equilibrium: $T_A\sin 60^\circ + T_B\sin 30^\circ = mg = 50\text{ N}$.
Solves the linear system to obtain $T_A = 0.5 P + 25\sqrt{3}$ and $T_B = 25 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} P$.

hints: Substitute the formulas for $T_A$ and $T_B$ into the condition $T_A = 2 T_B$.
Set $0.5 P + 25\sqrt{3} = 2\left(25 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} P\right) = 50 - \sqrt{3} P$.
Collect like terms in $P$: $(0.5 + \sqrt{3}) P = 50 - 25\sqrt{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute expressions from part (a) into $T_A = 2 T_B$:
$$0.5 P + 25\sqrt{3} = 2\left(25 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} P\right)$$
$$0.5 P + 25\sqrt{3} = 50 - \sqrt{3} P$$

Collect terms involving $P$ on the left-hand side:
$$(0.5 + \sqrt{3}) P = 50 - 25\sqrt{3}$$
$$P = \frac{50 - 25\sqrt{3}}{0.5 + \sqrt{3}}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up the target ratio condition:
- We want string $OA$ to carry twice the tension of string $OB$:
$$T_A = 2 T_B$$

Substitute the parametric formulas found in part (a):
$$0.5 P + 25\sqrt{3} = 2\left(25 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} P\right) = 50 - \sqrt{3} P$$
Rearrange to isolate $P$:
$$(0.5 + \sqrt{3}) P = 50 - 25\sqrt{3}$$

Calculate the required pull:
$$P = \frac{6.699}{2.232} \approx 3.00\text{ N}$$
A modest rightward pull of $3.00\text{ N}$ causes string $OA$ to support double the tension of string $OB$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 2: Multi-string junction under variable horizontal load and slack condition

hints: A string becomes slack when its tension drops to zero: $T_B = 0$.
From part (a), set $T_B = 25 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} P = 0 \implies P_{\max} = \frac{50}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{50\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 28.9\text{ N}$.
When string $OB$ is slack ($T_B = 0$), string $OA$ alone supports the entire vertical weight: $T_A\sin 60^\circ = 50$.
Calculate $T_A = \frac{50}{\sin 60^\circ} = \frac{100}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{100\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 57.7\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the condition for string $OB$ to become slack:
A string cannot exert a compressive force; it remains taut only while $T_B \geqslant 0$. At the verge of becoming slack:
$$T_B = 0 \implies 25 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} P = 0$$
$$P_{\max} = \frac{25 \times 2}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{50}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{50\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 28.8675 \approx 28.9\text{ N}$$

Calculate the tension $T_A$ in this limiting state:
With $T_B = 0$, string $OA$ supports the entire vertical weight:
$$\Sigma F_y = T_A\sin 60^\circ - 50 = 0$$
$$T_A = \frac{50}{\sin 60^\circ} = \frac{50}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} = \frac{100}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{100\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 57.7350 \approx 57.7\text{ N}$$

Confirm horizontal equilibrium in the limiting state:
$$\Sigma F_x = T_A\cos 60^\circ - P_{\max} = \left(\frac{100\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)(0.5) - \frac{50\sqrt{3}}{3} = 0\text{ N}$$
This confirms the limiting values: $P_{\max} = 28.9\text{ N}$ and $T_A = 57.7\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Understand the physical boundary condition:
- Strings can only pull, never push: $T_B \geqslant 0$.
- As the rightward pull $P$ increases, the junction is dragged further to the right.
- Eventually string $OB$ goes limp (slack) when $T_B = 0$:
$$25 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}P = 0 \implies P_{\max} = \frac{50\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 28.9\text{ N}$$

Find the resulting tension in the remaining taut string:
- Once string $OB$ is slack, string $OA$ is the only upward support:
$$T_A\sin 60^\circ = 50\text{ N}$$
$$T_A = \frac{50}{\sin 60^\circ} = \frac{100\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 57.7\text{ N}$$

Summarize the mechanical behavior:
- Any horizontal pull exceeding $28.9\text{ N}$ will cause the junction to swing past string $OB$, rendering string $OB$ completely inactive:
$$P > 28.9\text{ N} \implies T_B = 0$$
